questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) 3.0 (2026 to 2031, outlay about Rs 565.50 crore):
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme implemented by the Department of Land Resources.
2. It gives every land parcel a 14-digit Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN), also called Bhu-Aadhaar.
3. It is implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
Which of the above are correct?
questions.why: DILRMP is run by the Department of Land Resources (Ministry of Rural Development), not the Housing Ministry. The new phase also plans paperless registration and upgrades 75 Sub-Registrar Offices.
questions.insight: Land is a State subject (List II), so States build the land records and the Centre funds and standardises them.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (NCSK), consider the following statements:
1. It was set up under the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis Act, 1993.
2. It is a constitutional body under Article 338 of the Constitution.
3. It has continued to function through extensions by Government resolution since the Act lapsed in 2004.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The NCSK Act, 1993 lapsed on 29 February 2004, and the Commission has continued through extended resolutions since then, so it is non-statutory. Article 338 is for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes. The latest appointments run to 31 March 2028.
questions.insight: Article 338 is for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes; NCSK looks into the welfare of sanitation workers and manual scavengers.

src.name: PIB, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY), consider the following statements:
1. It is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme for small and marginal farmers.
2. The Centre matches the contribution made by the farmer.
3. It pays every landholding farmer Rs 6,000 a year in three instalments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: PM-KMY asks farmers aged 18 to 40 to pay Rs 55 to Rs 200 a month, matched by the Centre, for a minimum pension of Rs 3,000 a month at 60. The Rs 6,000 a year in three instalments is the income support of PM-KISAN, a different scheme.
questions.insight: Do not mix it up with PM-KISAN, which gives Rs 6,000 a year as income support.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The United Nations General Assembly, by a resolution passed in 2007, decided that the International Day of Democracy would be observed every year on:
questions.why: The 2007 resolution made 15 September the day, and it was first observed in 2008. 10 December is Human Rights Day.
questions.insight: In India, free and fair elections are part of the Constitution's basic structure.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the registration of political parties in India, consider the following statements:
1. Parties are registered with the Election Commission under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
2. A party must report to the Commission contributions above Rs 20,000 received from one donor in a year.
3. A party that is neither a national nor a State party is called a Registered Unrecognised Political Party.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Section 29A deals with registration, Section 29C with reporting of contributions above Rs 20,000, and a registered party without national or State recognition is a Registered Unrecognised Political Party (RUPP).
questions.insight: A registered party that is neither national nor State party is a Registered Unrecognised Political Party (RUPP).

src.name: Representation of the People Act, 1951 (India Code)

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the three-language formula in the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, consider the following statements:
1. Hindi must be taught in every State as one of the three languages.
2. States, schools and students may choose the three languages.
3. At least two of the three languages must be Indian languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: NEP 2020 keeps the formula but imposes no language on any State. The choice rests with States, schools and students, and at least two of the three languages must be Indian languages.
questions.insight: NEP 2020 also promotes teaching in the mother tongue or home language, at least up to Class 5.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Cabinet decision of September 2026 on the EPFO wage ceiling, consider the following statements:
1. The wage ceiling for mandatory coverage was raised from Rs 15,000 to Rs 21,000 a month.
2. It is the first revision of the ceiling since 2014.
3. Over 51 lakh more employees come under mandatory coverage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The ceiling rose from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 a month (Cabinet decision of 16 September, effective 17 September 2026). Government support for the Employees' Pension Scheme rises to about Rs 11,339 crore a year.
questions.insight: Total government support for the pension scheme (EPS) rises to about Rs 11,339 crore a year.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to India's real GDP growth for April to June 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Real GDP grew by 7.8%.
2. The growth was above the RBI's estimate of 7.0%.
3. The estimate is released by the Reserve Bank of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The National Statistics Office under MoSPI released the estimate: real GDP grew 7.8% (nominal 10.3%) and real GVA 8.2%, the highest Q1 growth of the last four years.
questions.insight: GDP is estimated by the National Statistics Office (NSO) under MoSPI.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to India's GDP series released by MoSPI in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The new series uses 2022-23 as its base year.
2. The new series replaced the 2004-05 series.
3. An updated series with new price indices was released on 31 August 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The new series, released on 27 February 2026, replaced the 2011-12 series, not the 2004-05 one. A base year is the benchmark used to measure real changes without the effect of inflation.
questions.insight: A base year is the benchmark year used to measure real changes without the effect of inflation.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the upgrade of India's long-term sovereign rating by Japan Credit Rating Agency (JCR) in September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The new rating is A- with a stable outlook.
2. The rating was raised from BBB+.
3. JCR also raised India's country ceiling to A.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. JCR cited steady growth and a sounder financial system. S&P and Morningstar DBRS (both BBB) had raised India's rating in 2025.
questions.insight: S&P (BBB) and Morningstar DBRS (BBB) raised India's rating in 2025 as well.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0, consider the following statements:
1. The Cabinet approved it on 5 May 2026.
2. It is operational until 31 March 2027, or until guarantees worth Rs 2.55 lakh crore are issued, whichever is earlier.
3. Scheduled passenger airlines get a 90% guarantee.
4. There is no cap on the guarantees that can be issued.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: The scheme is capped at Rs 2.55 lakh crore of guarantees and ends on 31 March 2027 if that cap is not reached earlier. Airlines also get additional credit up to Rs 1,500 crore per borrower. It runs through the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company.
questions.insight: ECLGS is run through the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC) via lending institutions.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auctions run by the RBI in September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The RBI lends money to banks in a VRRR auction to inject liquidity.
2. The rate in a VRRR is set by auction.
3. The VRRR is used to absorb excess liquidity from the banking system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: In a reverse repo the RBI borrows from banks, taking surplus liquidity out of the system. The VRRR cut-off rate was 5.24% in September 2026. The fixed-rate tools are the SDF, the floor of the corridor, and the repo rate.
questions.insight: The fixed-rate tools are the SDF (floor of the corridor) and the repo rate.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative, led by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade, is best described as:
opts: A World Trade Organization agreement on trade between the districts of its member countries
A new scheme that gives every district a fixed grant for its exports each financial year
A plan to set up a separate Special Economic Zone in every district of the whole country
A convergence framework drawing on existing schemes, grown out of One District One Product
questions.why: DEH makes each district a unit of export planning. District Export Promotion Committees prepare action plans and are a forum for exporters' grievances. DGFT works under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
questions.insight: DGFT works under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the World Economic Forum's Global Gender Gap Index 2026, consider the following statements:
1. India ranked 131st among 145 economies.
2. About 64.5% of India's gender gap has been closed.
3. The index measures four areas, one of which is defence participation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The four areas are economic participation, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment. Iceland ranked first for the 17th year, and the global gap is 69.2% closed.
questions.insight: The Index measures four areas: economic participation, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The 18th BRICS Summit, hosted by India in New Delhi on 12 and 13 September 2026, was held under which one of the following themes?
opts: Partnership for a Digital and Green Future for All Member Countries and Partners
Strengthening Global South Cooperation for Inclusive and Sustainable Governance
Peace, Security and Reformed Multilateralism for a Fairer International Order
Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability
questions.why: India holds the BRICS chair in 2026, and the summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration. India had earlier chaired BRICS in 2016 (Goa) and 2021 (virtual).
questions.insight: The previous summit's declaration (Rio de Janeiro, 2025) was titled on strengthening Global South cooperation.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, consider the following statements:
1. It was held in Tianjin, China, on 31 August and 1 September 2026.
2. It adopted the Bishkek Declaration.
3. India chaired the SCO in 2022-23.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The meeting was held in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. India backed proposals including making English an official SCO language, and the chair for 2026-27 passes to Pakistan.
questions.insight: India chaired the SCO in 2022-23 and hosted a virtual summit in 2023.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the award of the Court of Arbitration in the Indus Waters Western Rivers case at the end of August 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The Court held that the Indus Waters Treaty remains in force.
2. The Court held that the Treaty has stood terminated since April 2025.
3. The Treaty was signed in 1960, with the World Bank as a signatory.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Court held that the Treaty has not been terminated or suspended and that India's decision to place it in abeyance is not permissible under the Treaty or international law. India placed the Treaty in abeyance in April 2025.
questions.insight: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960 between India and Pakistan, with the World Bank as a signatory. India placed it in abeyance in April 2025.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the 'Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026' of the United States, consider the following statements:
1. It became law on 18 September 2026.
2. It lets the President impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods from the top five importers of Russian oil or gas.
3. It extends the Iran Sanctions Act to 2031.
4. The tariff power is automatic and does not depend on the President's decision.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: The tariff power is discretionary, not automatic. The Act passed the Senate 86-11 in August and became Public Law 119-111. It matters to India because India buys Russian crude oil, though the text does not name India.
questions.insight: It matters to India because India buys Russian crude oil, though the sources do not name India directly.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the GSLV-F17 mission launched from Sriharikota on 4 September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It carried EOS-05, described by ISRO as India's first imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit.
2. It was the 19th flight of the GSLV.
3. EOS-05 is a satellite of the NavIC navigation constellation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: EOS-05 is to be placed in the geostationary orbit at 85.5 degrees East after a series of orbit-raising burns. A geostationary satellite stays above one point of the equator because its orbit takes 24 hours.
questions.insight: A geostationary satellite stays above one point of the equator because its orbit takes 24 hours.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. They were notified in August 2026 to set one legal, traceable Indian Standard Time across the country.
2. They take effect immediately on publication.
3. CSIR-National Physical Laboratory provides the scientific basis for IST.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Rules take effect 180 days after publication. They cover the generation, maintenance and spread of IST, which is distributed through regional laboratories and ISRO's NavIC. India does not move to two time zones.
questions.insight: CSIR-National Physical Laboratory in New Delhi maintains India's national time standard.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan Awards, held in September 2026 on Swachh Vayu Diwas, consider the following statements:
1. Cities are ranked on the actions taken under their clean air plans.
2. Cities are ranked on their measured annual average PM2.5 levels.
3. Ward-level surveys covered over 7,400 wards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The ranking is based on reported implementation of city action plans under the National Clean Air Programme, not on pollution readings. 7 September is the International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies.
questions.insight: 7 September is the International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The UN General Assembly adopted the 'Correct the Map' resolution on 4 September 2026, which encourages the use of the Equal Earth and other equal-area maps.
Statement-II: The resolution is legally binding on all member states.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Statement-II is incorrect: the resolution is non-binding and was led by Togo and the African Union. The EU said it has no bearing on borders or sovereignty. The Mercator map stretches areas near the poles, which makes Africa look smaller than it is.
questions.insight: The Mercator map stretches areas near the poles, which makes Africa look smaller than it is.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: In the Global Financial Centres Index 40, published in September 2026, GIFT City was ranked:
questions.why: GFCI 40 was published on 16 September 2026 and covers 117 centres in its main index. GIFT City in Gujarat is India's first International Financial Services Centre and is regulated by the IFSCA.
questions.insight: GIFT City in Gujarat is India's first International Financial Services Centre, regulated by the IFSCA.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to India's nationwide HPV vaccination campaign launched in February 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It offers a free single dose to 14-year-old girls at government facilities.
2. It offers a free dose to all boys and girls at birth.
3. More than 80 lakh doses had been given by September 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The campaign was launched on 28 February 2026 from Ajmer for 14-year-old girls, not for newborns of both sexes. Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest coverage, with more than 22 lakh girls vaccinated.
questions.insight: Human papillomavirus causes most cases of cervical cancer, so vaccination before exposure is the best prevention.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider India's first soil carbon payments to farmers (September 2026):
1. They went to smallholders in Punjab and Haryana, with the first payments released at Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana.
2. They were made by the Grow Indigo programme with ICAR's technical guidance, with credits issued under the Verra VM0042 methodology.
3. They were paid from the Union Budget by the Ministry of Agriculture.
Which of the above are correct?
questions.why: The payments came from a private-led programme, not from the Union Budget. Farmers had adopted practices such as direct seeded rice, reduced tillage and crop residue management.
questions.insight: Soil carbon credits reward farming that stores more carbon in the soil or cuts emissions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to Naoero (formerly Nauru), which informed the United Nations in 2026 of its new official name, consider the following statements:
1. It lies in the south-western Pacific, in Micronesia, about 40 km south of the Equator.
2. It is a raised coral island.
3. Yaren is its official capital.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Naoero has no official capital; government offices are in Yaren. The island lies about 1,300 km north-east of the Solomon Islands. Its international code changes from NRU to NRO.
questions.insight: Its old name Nauru is replaced in the UN list, and its international code changes from NRU to NRO.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to Naoero (formerly Nauru), consider the following statements:
1. It is the world's smallest independent republic, covering about 21 sq km.
2. It is the third-smallest country after Vatican City and Monaco.
3. It is an archipelago of over 1,000 islands.
4. It has no rivers.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: Naoero is a single island with about 12,000 people. Its limited fresh water and phosphate mining shaped its economy and landscape.
questions.insight: It has no rivers; its limited fresh water and phosphate mining shaped the island's economy and landscape.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Albania
2. Serbia
3. Montenegro
4. Bulgaria
How many of the above share a border with Kosovo?
questions.why: Kosovo is a landlocked country in the central Balkans, bordered by Serbia, North Macedonia, Albania and Montenegro. Its capital is Pristina. It declared independence from Serbia on 17 February 2008, and India does not recognise it as an independent country.
questions.insight: Kosovo declared independence from Serbia on 17 February 2008. India does not recognise it as an independent country.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the river Yarlung Tsangpo, on which China has approved a large hydropower project, consider the following statements:
1. It flows east across Tibet, turns sharply south and enters India in Arunachal Pradesh as the Siang or Dihang.
2. It is called the Brahmaputra in Arunachal Pradesh and the Siang in Assam.
3. It is called the Jamuna in Bangladesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The river is the Siang in Arunachal Pradesh and becomes the Brahmaputra in Assam. India is a lower riparian state, so upstream dams raise questions about flow data and downstream impact.
questions.insight: India is a lower riparian state, so upstream dams raise questions about flow data and downstream impact.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Yarlung Tsangpo makes a sharp U-turn, known as the Great Bend, around which Himalayan peak in south-eastern Tibet?
questions.why: The Great Bend gorge is one of the deepest in the world, which is why it is considered for hydropower.
questions.insight: The Great Bend gorge is one of the deepest in the world, which is why it is considered for hydropower.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Lipulekh Pass is in Pithoragarh district of Uttarakhand, at the India-China-Nepal tri-junction.
Statement-II: The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra has used the Lipulekh route since 1954.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, but the Yatra's history does not explain the location. Nepal claims Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura, and India rejects the claim.
questions.insight: Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura are the territory Nepal claims.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Nathu La : Sikkim
2. Shipki La : Uttarakhand
3. Bomdi La : Himachal Pradesh
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.why: Shipki La is in Himachal Pradesh and Bomdi La is in Arunachal Pradesh. Zoji La is in Ladakh. Border trade and Kailash Mansarovar Yatra batches have used Nathu La and Lipulekh.
questions.insight: Border trade and Kailash Mansarovar Yatra batches have used Nathu La and Lipulekh.

src.name: MEA, Rajya Sabha reply on border trade

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the Strait of Hormuz, where disruptions in 2026 have affected trade, consider the following statements:
1. It links the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.
2. It lies between Oman and Iran.
3. It is the only sea route from the Persian Gulf to the open ocean.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Strait of Hormuz links the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman. Because much of the world's oil passes through it, ports outside it, such as Sohar, gain importance.
questions.insight: Because much of the world's oil passes through it, ports outside it, such as Sohar, gain importance.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Sohar Port, highlighted as a gateway that avoids the Strait of Hormuz under the India-Oman CEPA, is located on which one of the following?
opts: The Red Sea coast of Saudi Arabia, near the city of Jeddah
The Mediterranean coast of Egypt, near the city of Alexandria
The Persian Gulf, inside the Strait of Hormuz and its approaches
The Gulf of Oman, outside the Strait of Hormuz
questions.why: Sohar is in northern Oman, between Muscat and Dubai, and gives access to sea lanes without entering the Persian Gulf. The India-Oman CEPA came into force on 1 June 2026.
questions.insight: The India-Oman CEPA came into force on 1 June 2026.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Pakistan
2. Saudi Arabia
3. Iran
How many of the above border the Gulf of Oman?
questions.why: The Gulf of Oman is bordered by Oman, Iran, Pakistan and the United Arab Emirates. It is the north-western arm of the Arabian Sea.
questions.insight: It is the north-western arm of the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the El Niño that NOAA said in September 2026 may become very strong, consider the following statements:
1. It is an unusual warming of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean.
2. It weakens the trade winds and shifts rain away from the western Pacific.
3. It is an unusual cooling of the central equatorial Pacific Ocean.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The cooling phase is called La Niña. El Niño is the warm phase of the El Niño Southern Oscillation.
questions.insight: The opposite, cooler phase is called La Niña.

src.name: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, ENSO Diagnostic Discussion

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: El Niño years are generally associated with weaker rainfall in the Indian southwest monsoon.
Statement-II: Every El Niño year brings a drought in India.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Statement-II is incorrect: the link is a tendency, not a rule. Some El Niño years have normal rainfall, and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole can offset some of the effect.
questions.insight: The link is a tendency, not a rule: some El Niño years have normal rainfall.

src.name: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, ENSO Diagnostic Discussion

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the Niño 3.4 region used to monitor El Niño, consider the following statements:
1. It lies in the central equatorial Pacific, roughly 5°N to 5°S and 170°W to 120°W.
2. Its sea-surface temperature anomaly is the main index.
3. An anomaly above +0.5°C for several months signals El Niño conditions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. NOAA reported the anomaly at about +2.1°C in October 2026.
questions.insight: An anomaly above +0.5°C for several months signals El Niño conditions.

src.name: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, ENSO Diagnostic Discussion

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to IMD's classification of rainfall in 24 hours, consider the following statements:
1. Rainfall of 64.5 to 115.5 mm is 'heavy'.
2. Rainfall of 204.5 mm or more is 'extremely heavy'.
3. Rainfall of less than 64.5 mm is 'very heavy'.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: Rainfall of 115.6 to 204.4 mm is 'very heavy'. IMD recorded extremely heavy rain over Uttar Pradesh in late September 2026. Terai districts flood easily because the land is flat and rivers block drainage.
questions.insight: Terai districts flood easily because the land is flat and rivers block drainage.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to a Western Disturbance (WD), consider the following statements:
1. It is a summer wind that blows from the Thar desert.
2. It is an eastward-moving extratropical system that brings winter rain to north-west India.
3. It travels on the subtropical westerly jet stream.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: WDs draw moisture mainly from the Mediterranean and bring rain and snow to the western Himalayas and the north-western plains. When a WD meets a tropical system such as a depression, rain can become very heavy.
questions.insight: When a WD meets a tropical system such as a depression, rain can become very heavy.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In the IMD classification, a deep depression has sustained winds of 17 to 27 knots.
Statement-II: In the IMD classification, a depression has sustained winds of 17 to 27 knots.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Statement-I is incorrect. A deep depression has winds of 28 to 33 knots, a cyclonic storm 34 to 47 knots and a severe cyclonic storm 48 to 63 knots. IMD tracked a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal in late September 2026.
questions.insight: IMD tracked a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal in late September 2026.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the Terai region, consider the following statements:
1. It is a low-lying marshy belt south of the Bhabar, along the Himalayan foothills.
2. It is a coral reef region in the Bay of Bengal.
3. Streams that sink in the Bhabar re-emerge in it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Flat terrain and a high water table make waterlogging common in the Terai after heavy rain, so it is prone to floods in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
questions.insight: Flat terrain and a high water table make waterlogging common after heavy rain.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Mercator projection preserves local shapes but exaggerates areas near the poles.
Statement-II: The Mercator projection is a cylindrical, conformal projection.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Being conformal, it preserves angles, but this stretches areas near the poles, so Africa looks smaller than it is. The UN resolution of 4 September 2026 encourages the Equal Earth map, an equal-area projection from 2018.
questions.insight: Equal Earth (2018) is an equal-area projection that keeps relative sizes correct.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: On a true-area basis, Africa is about how many times larger than Greenland, which looks similar in size on a Mercator map?
questions.why: Africa covers about 30.4 million sq km, while Greenland covers about 2.2 million sq km. Mercator makes high-latitude landmasses look much larger.
questions.insight: Mercator makes high-latitude landmasses look much larger.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to Mayun (Perim) Island, consider the following statements:
1. It lies in the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.
2. The strait lies between Yemen and Djibouti.
3. The island belongs to Yemen.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Bab-el-Mandeb links the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden and guards a key route for Suez Canal traffic.
questions.insight: The Suez Canal joins the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the Suez Canal, consider the following statements:
1. It links the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea.
2. It shortens the sea route between Europe and Asia.
3. It links the Atlantic and the Pacific Oceans.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Panama Canal, not the Suez Canal, links the Atlantic and the Pacific.
questions.insight: The Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The southwest monsoon normally begins to withdraw from north-west India, around mid-September.
Statement-II: Tamil Nadu receives its main rain from the retreating north-east monsoon from October.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, but one does not explain the other. The monsoon advances from the south and retreats from the north-west, with withdrawal usually starting in September.
questions.insight: Tamil Nadu receives its main rain from the retreating (north-east) monsoon from October.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the Sone (Son) river, consider the following statements:
1. It rises near Amarkantak.
2. It joins the Ganga near Allahabad.
3. It joins the Ganga from the right (south) bank.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Son joins the Ganga near Patna in Bihar. The Ghaghara, Gandak and Kosi are left-bank tributaries of the Ganga.
questions.insight: Left-bank tributaries of the Ganga include the Ghaghara, Gandak and Kosi.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the subtropical westerly jet stream, consider the following statements:
1. It is a fast, narrow band of upper-air winds blowing west to east.
2. It is found in the upper troposphere.
3. It carries Western Disturbances to India.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: In winter it lies south of the Himalayas, steering disturbances towards north India. In summer it shifts north of the Himalayas, which helps the monsoon set in.
questions.insight: In summer it shifts north of the Himalayas, which helps the monsoon set in.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A 'hanging glacier' is best described as which one of the following?
opts: A glacier that has melted completely and left only a bare rock valley behind it in the mountains
A glacier that flows all the way down into the sea and breaks off into icebergs there
A glacier that is formed only in the Antarctic region and is never found anywhere else in the world
A tributary glacier that ends abruptly above the main valley glacier or on a cliff
questions.why: Hanging glaciers sit high on steep slopes, so ice can break off and fall, which is a hazard in the Himalayas. Rapid warming can destabilise them and trigger avalanches and glacial floods.
questions.insight: Rapid warming can destabilise them and trigger avalanches and glacial floods.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: In the Himalayas, which belt of porous pebbly deposits lies at the foot of the Shiwaliks and absorbs the streams that come down?
questions.why: Streams sink into the coarse Bhabar and re-emerge in the Terai. Bhangar and Khadar are old and new alluvium of the plains. The Bhabar is not good for farming but is important for groundwater recharge.
questions.insight: Bhabar is not good for farming but is important for groundwater recharge.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to 'The Painted Haveli Towns of Shekhawati', which India submitted to UNESCO on 1 June 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It has been placed on India's Tentative List for World Heritage nomination.
2. The serial entry covers 14 towns in Jhunjhunu, Churu and Sikar in Rajasthan.
3. It has been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: A Tentative List is a country's inventory of sites it intends to nominate; being on it is a required step before a full nomination, so the site is not yet inscribed. It was submitted under cultural criteria (iii), (iv) and (v).
questions.insight: It was submitted under cultural criteria (iii), (iv) and (v).

src.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Tentative Lists

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q: The painted havelis of Shekhawati in Rajasthan are known for which one of the following?
opts: Rock-cut Buddhist caves carved into the hills by monks and royal patrons during the early centuries of the Common Era
Wooden temples of the Himalayas, built by hill chieftains using deodar timber and carved roof panels
Stepwells of the Chalukya period, built by kings to store water for towns in the dry western regions
Frescoes on the walls of merchants' mansions, built mainly from the mid-19th century to the 1930s
questions.why: Marwari merchants who earned wealth in colonial cities built richly painted havelis in their home towns such as Mandawa, Nawalgarh and Fatehpur. The region is often called an open-air art gallery.
questions.insight: The region is often called an open-air art gallery.

src.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Tentative Lists

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
Consider the following UNESCO World Heritage criteria:
1. Criterion (iv): an outstanding example of a type of building or architectural ensemble
2. Criterion (vii): superlative natural phenomena
3. Criterion (x): significant natural habitats for biodiversity
How many of the above are used to judge a cultural site such as the Shekhawati towns?
questions.why: Criteria (i) to (vi) are cultural and (vii) to (x) are natural. Shekhawati was proposed under (iii), (iv) and (v). A site needs to show 'Outstanding Universal Value' to be inscribed.
questions.insight: A site needs to show 'Outstanding Universal Value' to be inscribed.

src.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Tentative Lists

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to Hindi Diwas, observed on 14 September, consider the following statements:
1. It marks the day in 1949 when the Eighth Schedule was added to the Constitution.
2. It marks the day in 1949 when the Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi in the Devanagari script as the Union's official language.
3. Article 343 declares Hindi in Devanagari as the official language of the Union.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Eighth Schedule lists recognised languages and was part of the Constitution as adopted. India has no 'national language' in the Constitution; Hindi is the official language of the Union. The 6th All India Official Language Conference was held in 2026.
questions.insight: India has no 'national language' in the Constitution; Hindi is the official language of the Union.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution directs the Union to promote the spread of the Hindi language?
questions.why: Article 343 deals with the official language itself and Article 348 with the language of the courts. The Eighth Schedule lists 22 recognised languages.
questions.insight: The Eighth Schedule lists 22 recognised languages.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Munshi-Ayyangar formula of the Constituent Assembly provided for Hindi in Devanagari as the official language, with English continuing for 15 years.
Statement-II: The compromise settled a long debate between supporters of Hindi and those wanting English or regional languages to continue.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: The Official Languages Act, 1963 later allowed English to continue even beyond 1965.
questions.insight: The Official Languages Act, 1963 later allowed English to continue even beyond 1965.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to the Cabinet Mission of 1946, consider the following statements:
1. It proposed a three-tier federation with provincial groups.
2. It proposed the immediate partition of India into two countries.
3. Its members were Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Mission rejected the demand for a separate Pakistan. It proposed a weak Centre, provinces in Groups A, B and C, and a Constituent Assembly elected by provincial legislatures.
questions.insight: Its members were Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. It lists the languages recognised by the Constitution.
2. It has 22 languages today.
3. Dogri, Bodo, Maithili and Santhali were added by the 92nd Amendment in 2003.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Tulu is a major language that is not yet in the Eighth Schedule. The Seventh Schedule, not the Eighth, lists the Union, State and Concurrent subjects.
questions.insight: Tulu is a major language that is not yet in the Eighth Schedule.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Tulu language, consider the following statements:
1. It is a Dravidian language.
2. It has its own old script, Tigalari.
3. It is spoken mainly in the Konkan region of Maharashtra.
4. It is included in the Eighth Schedule.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: Tulu is spoken mainly in coastal Karnataka (Dakshina Kannada and Udupi) and northern Kerala (Kasaragod). People have long demanded its inclusion in the Eighth Schedule.
questions.insight: People have long demanded its inclusion in the Eighth Schedule.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Dogri, whose traditional script is called Dogra Akkhar, was added to the Eighth Schedule by which one of the following?
questions.why: The 2003 amendment added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali. The 21st Amendment (1967) added Sindhi, and the 71st (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali.
questions.insight: The 21st Amendment (1967) added Sindhi; the 71st (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to Rani Avantibai Lodhi, consider the following statements:
1. She was the queen of Jhansi.
2. She rejected the British Court of Wards.
3. She defeated the British in the Battle of Kheri in November 1857.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: She was the queen of Ramgarh (in present-day Madhya Pradesh), not Jhansi. She died in March 1858 rather than surrender.
questions.insight: She defeated the British in the Battle of Kheri in November 1857 and died in March 1858 rather than surrender.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Under the Court of Wards policy, the British took over the administration of an estate whose ruler was seen as unfit or a minor.
Statement-II: Under the Court of Wards policy, the ruler of the estate was made the head of a court.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Statement-II is incorrect. The policy often led to annexation or resentment, as in Rani Avantibai's Ramgarh. The Doctrine of Lapse (Dalhousie) was a related annexation tool.
questions.insight: The Doctrine of Lapse (Dalhousie) was a related annexation tool.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to Vinoba Bhave, consider the following statements:
1. He started the Bhoodan Movement in 1951 at Pochampally.
2. Gandhi chose him as the first individual satyagrahi in 1940.
3. He received the Bharat Ratna in 1958.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: He received the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 1958 and the Bharat Ratna in 1983. Bhoodan asked landowners to donate land for the landless.
questions.insight: He received the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 1958 and the Bharat Ratna in 1983.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Vinoba Bhave's movement that followed Bhoodan, in which villages were given up for common ownership, was called:
questions.why: Gramdan villages were meant to hold land in common. Bhoodan began in 1951 and Gramdan became its main form from the late 1950s.
questions.insight: Bhoodan began in 1951 and Gramdan became its main form from the late 1950s.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay, born on 15 September 1876, consider the following statements:
1. He was a Bengali novelist.
2. He wrote Devdas and Parineeta.
3. His novel Pather Dabi was banned by the British government in 1927.
4. He was a Hindi poet of the Chhayavad school.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: Devdas was written in 1917, and Pather Dabi is about a revolutionary secret society. He was not a Hindi poet.
questions.insight: Pather Dabi is about a revolutionary secret society.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar), born on 17 September 1879, consider the following statements:
1. He founded the Self-Respect Movement in 1925.
2. He founded the Arya Samaj in 1875.
3. He founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Arya Samaj was founded by Dayananda Saraswati and the Satyashodhak Samaj by Jyotiba Phule. Periyar later led the Dravidar Kazhagam (1944), and his journal Kudi Arasu (1925) spread the movement's ideas.
questions.insight: His journal Kudi Arasu (1925) spread the movement's ideas.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to the Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25), consider the following statements:
1. It was a protest for the right of lower castes to use roads near the Vaikom temple in Kerala.
2. It was a protest against the salt tax.
3. Gandhi supported it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It was one of the first campaigns against untouchability and caste restrictions on public roads, and Periyar took part. The Temple Entry Proclamation in Travancore followed in 1936.
questions.insight: The Temple Entry Proclamation in Travancore followed in 1936.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Which one of the following parties was formed in 1944 from the Justice Party under Periyar's leadership?
questions.why: The Justice Party, formed in 1916 to represent non-Brahmins in Madras Presidency, was renamed Dravidar Kazhagam in 1944. The DMK split off from it in 1949 under C.N. Annadurai.
questions.insight: Later, the DMK split off from it in 1949 under C.N. Annadurai.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to Bhagat Singh, born on 28 September 1907, consider the following statements:
1. He was a leader of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association, formed in 1928.
2. He and B.K. Dutt threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929.
3. He was executed on 23 March 1931, observed as Shaheed Diwas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. He worked with Chandrashekhar Azad and others.
questions.insight: He was executed on 23 March 1931, observed as Shaheed Diwas.

src.name: PIB, Prime Minister's tribute on Shaheed Diwas

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad', made popular by Bhagat Singh, was first raised by which one of the following?
questions.why: The Urdu poet and freedom fighter Hasrat Mohani coined it in 1921. Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt shouted it after the Assembly bomb on 8 April 1929.
questions.insight: Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt shouted it after the Assembly bomb on 8 April 1929.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to Bhagat Singh's Naujawan Bharat Sabha, consider the following statements:
1. It was formed in 1926 in Lahore.
2. It was formed by Subhas Chandra Bose.
3. It encouraged young people to join the freedom struggle with a socialist and secular outlook.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: The Sabha was formed by Bhagat Singh and his comrades. The Lahore Conspiracy Case trial followed the killing of the police officer Saunders in December 1928.
questions.insight: The Lahore Conspiracy Case trial followed the killing of the police officer Saunders in December 1928.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai started the Bengal Chemical works in 1906.
Statement-II: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai challenged the British shipping monopoly.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Statement-I is incorrect: in 1906 he started the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company between Tuticorin and Colombo. He was called 'Kappalottiya Tamizhan' (the Tamil helmsman) and was jailed in 1908 for sedition.
questions.insight: He was jailed in 1908 for sedition after supporting a strike in Tuticorin.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to 'Vande Mataram', whose 150 years of composition are being commemorated, consider the following statements:
1. It was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in 1905.
2. It was later included in his novel Anandamath.
3. It was adopted as the national song on 24 January 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It was composed in 1875 and first sung at the Congress session of 1896 by Rabindranath Tagore. The Government is holding a year-long commemoration.
questions.insight: The Government is holding a year-long commemoration.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is India's highest award in cinema and was first given in 1969.
Statement-II: The first recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award was Devika Rani.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, but the first recipient's name does not explain the year of the award. The 2024 award went to actor Anant Nag, at the 72nd National Film Awards presented on 22 September 2026. The Directorate of Film Festivals runs the awards.
questions.insight: The awards are run by the Directorate of Film Festivals under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
Consider the following classical dances:
1. Kathakali
2. Kuchipudi
3. Odissi
How many of the above are from Kerala?
questions.why: Kathakali is from Kerala, Kuchipudi from Andhra Pradesh and Odissi from Odisha. Kathakali tells stories from the epics through elaborate makeup, costumes and hand gestures.
questions.insight: Odissi is from Odisha, Manipuri from Manipur and Kuchipudi from Andhra Pradesh.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
Consider the following ports of ancient India:
1. Muziris
2. Tamralipti
3. Lothal
4. Broach (Bharuch)
How many of the above were major ports on the Malabar coast trading with the Roman world?
questions.why: Muziris, near Kodungallur in Kerala, traded spices and pepper for Roman gold. Lothal was a Harappan dockyard in Gujarat, and Tamralipti was a port on the Bengal coast.
questions.insight: Lothal was a Harappan dockyard in Gujarat, and Tamralipti was a port on the Bengal coast.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Harappan dockyard at Lothal, a sign of ancient India's maritime trade, is located in which one of the following States?
questions.why: Lothal is near the Gulf of Khambhat. Harappans traded with Mesopotamia through the Persian Gulf.
questions.insight: Harappans traded with Mesopotamia through the Persian Gulf.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to the 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea', consider the following statements:
1. It is a first-century CE Greek guide to sea trade routes, ports and goods.
2. It is an inscription of Ashoka.
3. It is a key source for Indo-Roman trade.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It lists ports and trade goods of the Red Sea, Arabia and India, including those of the Indian coasts.
questions.insight: It is a key source for Indo-Roman trade.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched on an ISRO GSLV from Sriharikota on 30 August 2026.
2. It launched from Launch Complex 39A in Florida on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy.
3. It is travelling to an orbit around the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The telescope launched on 30 August 2026 on a Falcon Heavy from Florida, not from India. NASA said its first images are expected by early 2027.
questions.insight: NASA said first images are expected by early 2027.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The Sun-Earth L2 point, where the Roman telescope is headed, is located at which one of the following places?
opts: On the surface of the Moon, at the centre of its far side hemisphere
In low Earth orbit at an altitude of about 400 km above the ground
Between the Earth and the Sun, about 1.5 million km from Earth on the sunward side
About 1.5 million km from Earth, on the side away from the Sun
questions.why: At L2 the Sun, Earth and Moon are all on the same side, which makes shielding and cooling easier for infrared telescopes. The James Webb Space Telescope is also at L2.
questions.insight: The James Webb Space Telescope is also at L2, and India's Aditya-L1 is at the Sun-Earth L1 point.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following objectives:
1. Studying dark energy
2. Surveying the sky in infrared over a wide field
3. Detecting gravitational waves from the ground
How many of the above are the main objectives of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope?
questions.why: Roman also hunts for exoplanets. Its mirror is about the same size as Hubble's but it has a much wider field of view. It is named after NASA's first Chief of Astronomy, called the 'Mother of Hubble'.
questions.insight: It is named after NASA's first Chief of Astronomy, Nancy Grace Roman, called the 'Mother of Hubble'.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India's solar mission Aditya-L1 is placed near the Sun-Earth L1 point.
Statement-II: The L1 point lies between the Sun and Earth, about 1.5 million km from Earth, and gives an uninterrupted view of the Sun.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: The position at L1 is what allows continuous observation of the Sun. L2, on the far side of the Earth from the Sun, suits deep-space telescopes.
questions.insight: L2, on the far side, suits deep-space telescopes.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the first high-value agreement signed by DRDO under the Technology Development Fund (TDF) in September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It is to develop an indigenous 20 mK dilution refrigerator for quantum applications.
2. It was signed with a start-up, Zero mK India Pvt Ltd.
3. The TDF is a Ministry of Defence programme run by DRDO to involve start-ups, MSMEs and industry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The agreement comes under the Rs 500 crore deep-tech corpus of the TDF.
questions.insight: TDF is a Ministry of Defence programme run by DRDO to involve start-ups, MSMEs and industry.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: With reference to quantum computing, why is a dilution refrigerator needed for a superconducting quantum computer, such as the one DRDO plans to build indigenously?
opts: It supplies the electricity that the processors need to run their calculations without any break
It cools the laboratory room in which the engineers and technicians work on the computer each day
It stores the large amounts of data that the quantum computer processes during its calculations
Qubits need extremely low temperatures, close to absolute zero, to keep their quantum states
questions.why: Heat disturbs fragile quantum states, so superconducting qubits are kept at millikelvin temperatures. Absolute zero is 0 K, which is -273.15 degrees Celsius.
questions.insight: Absolute zero is 0 K, which is -273.15 degrees Celsius.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: A temperature of 20 millikelvin is closest to which one of the following?
questions.why: 20 mK is 0.02 K above absolute zero (-273.15 degrees Celsius), so it is about -273.13 degrees Celsius. Kelvin has no negative values.
questions.insight: Kelvin has no negative values; zero kelvin is absolute zero.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the National Quantum Mission, approved by the Cabinet in April 2023, consider the following statements:
1. It has an outlay of about Rs 6,003.65 crore for 2023-24 to 2030-31.
2. It is run by the Indian Space Research Organisation.
3. It supports four Thematic Hubs, including one at IISc Bengaluru for quantum computing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Mission is run by the Department of Science and Technology. The other hubs are IIT Madras with C-DoT (communication), IIT Bombay (sensing and metrology) and IIT Delhi (materials and devices). The goal is intermediate-scale quantum computers with 50 to 1,000 physical qubits.
questions.insight: The goal is to build intermediate-scale quantum computers with 50 to 1,000 physical qubits.

src.name: DST, Cabinet approves National Quantum Mission

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), consider the following statements:
1. It uses quantum properties of light particles to share a secret key.
2. Any attempt to eavesdrop disturbs the quantum states and can be detected.
3. It sends data faster than the speed of light.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: Nothing travels faster than light, and QKD does not change this. India's National Quantum Mission includes quantum communication as one of its four verticals.
questions.insight: India's National Quantum Mission includes quantum communication as one of its four verticals.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Biovigilance Programme of India, approved by the Government in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It is meant to monitor adverse events linked to organ and tissue transplantation.
2. It is led by the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission.
3. It is meant to track diseases in cattle.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It joins the Pharmacovigilance Programme for medicines and the Materiovigilance Programme for medical devices. The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission is at Ghaziabad.
questions.insight: The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission, at Ghaziabad, publishes the Indian Pharmacopoeia.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Pharmacovigilance is the science of detecting and preventing adverse effects of medicines.
Statement-II: Materiovigilance does the same for medical devices.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, but one does not explain the other. The Pharmacovigilance Programme of India, coordinated by the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission, records adverse drug reactions.
questions.insight: Materiovigilance does the same for medical devices.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam, consider the following statements:
1. It attained first criticality in April 2020.
2. A fast breeder reactor produces more fissile material than it consumes.
3. It belongs to the second stage of India's three-stage nuclear programme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: PFBR, built by BHAVINI, attained first criticality on 6 April 2026. Its blanket is designed to hold thorium-232, which turns into uranium-233. Kalpakkam is in Tamil Nadu.
questions.insight: Kalpakkam is in Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Pressurised heavy water reactors using natural uranium
2. Fast breeder reactors making plutonium and uranium-233
3. Fusion reactors
4. Thorium and uranium-233 cycles
How many of the above are stages of India's three-stage nuclear power programme?
questions.why: Stage one uses PHWRs on natural uranium, stage two uses fast breeders, and stage three uses thorium and uranium-233 cycles. India has large thorium reserves in monazite sands.
questions.insight: India has large thorium reserves in monazite sands.

src.name: PIB, Nuclear Energy Technology in India

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Thorium-232 is not fissile, but it is useful as a nuclear fuel.
Statement-II: When thorium-232 absorbs a neutron, it changes into fissile uranium-233.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Thorium is a fertile material, which breeds new fuel. Fissile materials such as U-233, U-235 and Pu-239 sustain the chain reaction. India follows a closed fuel cycle, reprocessing spent fuel to reuse materials.
questions.insight: India follows a closed fuel cycle, reprocessing spent fuel to reuse materials.

src.name: PIB, Nuclear Energy Technology in India

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to National Space Day, consider the following statements:
1. It is observed on 23 August.
2. On 23 August 2023, Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's south pole.
3. The 3rd National Space Day in 2026 was held at Bengaluru.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The 3rd National Space Day in 2026 was held at Ahmedabad, with the theme 'Towards Viksit Bharat: Innovating, Collaborating and Aspiring to Global Space Leadership'. India became the fourth country to land on the Moon and the first near the south pole.
questions.insight: India was the first country to land near the lunar south pole.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The landing spot of Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander on the Moon was named which one of the following?
questions.why: The name was announced on 26 August 2023. The Chandrayaan-2 impact site is called Tiranga Point, and the Pragyan rover explored the area around Shiv Shakti Point.
questions.insight: The Pragyan rover explored the area around Shiv Shakti Point.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India's GSLV uses only solid fuel in all its stages.
Statement-II: The GSLV is a three-stage vehicle with an indigenous cryogenic third stage, suited to geosynchronous transfer orbits.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Statement-I is incorrect: the cryogenic third stage uses liquid fuel. The GSLV puts heavier satellites into higher orbits than the PSLV, which is mainly used for polar and sun-synchronous orbits.
questions.insight: PSLV is mainly used for polar and sun-synchronous orbits.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: NavIC, whose signals help distribute Indian Standard Time, stands for which one of the following?
opts: Naval Intelligence Command for Indian Coasts
Network for Indian Cellular communication towers
questions.why: NavIC is India's regional satellite navigation system and covers India and about 1,500 km around it. ISRO's satellites carry atomic clocks, and the Legal Metrology (IST) Rules, 2026 use NavIC and CSIR-NPL for traceable time.
questions.insight: The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 use NavIC and CSIR-NPL for traceable time.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to India's first hydrogen train, flagged off on 17 July 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It runs between Jind and Sonipat in Haryana.
2. It is powered by overhead electric lines only.
3. The route is about 89 km long.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The train is powered by hydrogen fuel cells, which combine hydrogen and oxygen to make electricity with water as the only by-product. Jind has a hydrogen facility storing about 3,000 kg, and the operating speed is 75 km/h.
questions.insight: The route is about 89 km, with an operating speed of 75 km/h.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The National Green Hydrogen Mission, approved in January 2023, aims for at least 5 million tonnes of green hydrogen production a year by 2030.
Statement-II: Green hydrogen is produced from natural gas.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Statement-II is incorrect. Green hydrogen is made by splitting water with renewable electricity, so it produces no carbon dioxide. Grey hydrogen comes from natural gas, and blue hydrogen captures its carbon.
questions.insight: Grey hydrogen comes from natural gas, and blue hydrogen captures its carbon.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Rs 7,280 crore scheme for sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnets (REPM), consider the following statements:
1. It aims to build 6,000 tonnes a year of integrated magnet capacity in India.
2. Five beneficiaries are to be chosen by global bidding.
3. It has sales-linked incentives of Rs 6,450 crore.
4. It has a capital subsidy of Rs 7,280 crore.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: The capital subsidy is Rs 750 crore; Rs 7,280 crore is the total outlay. India imports all its sintered NdFeB magnets now. The Ministry of Heavy Industries extended the bid timeline in July 2026.
questions.insight: The Ministry of Heavy Industries extended the bid timeline in July 2026.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following uses:
1. Electric vehicle motors
2. Wind turbines
3. Fertiliser production
How many of the above are major uses of rare earth permanent magnets (NdFeB)?
questions.why: NdFeB magnets are among the strongest magnets, so they make motors lighter and more efficient. 'Rare earths' are 17 elements: the 15 lanthanides plus scandium and yttrium.
questions.insight: 'Rare earths' are 17 elements: the 15 lanthanides plus scandium and yttrium.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number of a mobile phone, consider the following statements:
1. It is a 10-digit number that identifies the SIM card.
2. The Sanchar Saathi portal and the CEIR use it to block lost or stolen phones.
3. Tampering with IMEI numbers is prohibited under the 2025 Telecom Cyber Security Rules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The IMEI is a unique 15-digit number that identifies the handset, not the SIM card. Dialling *#06# usually shows it.
questions.insight: Dialling *#06# usually shows the IMEI.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the BioE3 policy (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment), approved in 2024, consider the following statements:
1. It supports biomanufacturing of bio-based chemicals, enzymes and biopolymers.
2. It is implemented by the Department of Biotechnology and BIRAC.
3. Projects under it aim to make PLA and PHA as import substitutes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Polylactic acid (PLA) is made from plant sugars, for instance from corn or sugarcane, and is biodegradable under industrial composting.
questions.insight: Polylactic acid (PLA) is made from plant sugars, for instance from corn or sugarcane, and is biodegradable under industrial composting.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to a plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV), consider the following statements:
1. It has both a petrol or diesel engine and a battery that can be charged from an external plug.
2. It can run a short distance on its battery and switch to the engine for longer trips.
3. A battery electric vehicle has an engine in addition to its battery.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: A battery electric vehicle (BEV) has no engine, and a strong hybrid cannot be plugged in.
questions.insight: A battery electric vehicle (BEV) has no engine, and a strong hybrid cannot be plugged in.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the yeast Candida auris, consider the following statements:
1. It is a virus that causes seasonal flu.
2. It resists many antifungal drugs and spreads in hospitals.
3. The World Health Organization lists it in its critical priority group of fungal pathogens.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: C. auris is a yeast, not a virus. Overuse of antifungals in agriculture and medicine is a driver of resistance.
questions.insight: Overuse of antifungals in agriculture and medicine is a driver of resistance.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) of the European Union, consider the following statements:
1. Its transitional, reporting-only phase ran from 2023 to 2025.
2. Its definitive phase began on 1 January 2026.
3. Importers have had to pay the full carbon charge since the first day of 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The payment obligation is phased in up to 2034, and EU certificate sales for CBAM begin in 2027. India is preparing for CBAM because its steel and aluminium exports to the EU are the most exposed.
questions.insight: EU certificate sales for CBAM begin in 2027.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following goods:
1. Cement
2. Textiles
3. Aluminium
4. Hydrogen
How many of the above are covered by the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism of the European Union?
questions.why: CBAM covers cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen. It prices the carbon embedded in carbon-intensive imports, and importers of more than 50 tonnes of covered goods need authorisation.
questions.insight: India's steel and aluminium exports to the EU are most exposed.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: 'Carbon leakage', the problem the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism is meant to address, refers to which one of the following?
opts: Escape of carbon dioxide from storage tanks and pipelines used in carbon capture and storage projects
Loss of carbon credits from the accounts of firms because of errors in measuring and reporting emissions
Release of the carbon stored in forests when fires burn large areas of woodland in the dry season
Industries moving to countries with weaker carbon rules, shifting emissions rather than cutting them
questions.why: If producers move to places with no carbon price, global emissions may not fall, and a border tax puts imports on equal terms. Critics call CBAM a trade barrier that conflicts with the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities.
questions.insight: Critics call CBAM a trade barrier and say it conflicts with the principle of 'common but differentiated responsibilities'.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), consider the following statements:
1. It is set up under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
2. It is run by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency.
3. It sets emission-intensity targets for energy-intensive sectors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The scheme is set up under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, as amended in 2022. A domestic carbon price may help Indian exporters show that they already pay for carbon.
questions.insight: A domestic carbon price may help Indian exporters show they already pay for carbon.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
India launched a Net Zero Portal and an NAPCC Dashboard on World Ozone Day 2026. Consider the following:
1. Solar energy
2. Smart cities
3. Green India
How many of the above were among the eight national missions of the National Action Plan on Climate Change launched in 2008?
questions.why: The original eight missions are solar energy, enhanced energy efficiency, sustainable habitat, water, Himalayan ecosystem, Green India, sustainable agriculture and strategic knowledge. The dashboard tracks the missions across States and Union Territories.
questions.insight: The dashboard tracks progress of the missions across States and Union Territories.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: World Ozone Day, observed on 16 September, commemorates the signing of the Montreal Protocol in 1987.
Statement-II: The Kigali Amendment (2016) extended the Montreal Protocol to hydrofluorocarbons, which are powerful greenhouse gases.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, but the Kigali Amendment came 29 years later and does not explain the choice of the day. India ratified the Kigali Amendment in 2021.
questions.insight: India ratified the Kigali Amendment in 2021.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to Project Cheetah, consider the following statements, based on the Government's update of May 2026:
1. India had about 53 cheetahs, of which 33 were born in India.
2. Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh is the primary site.
3. Nine cheetahs arrived from Botswana in February 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary is being prepared as additional habitat, and the first recorded birth in the wild took place in April 2026.
questions.insight: The first recorded birth in the wild took place in April 2026.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Project Cheetah reintroduced cheetahs to India from Namibia in September 2022. In which year was the cheetah declared extinct in India?
questions.why: The Asiatic cheetah vanished from India by the mid-20th century. The animals brought in belong to the African subspecies, and the Asiatic cheetah survives today only in Iran.
questions.insight: The Asiatic cheetah survives today only in Iran.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following sites:
1. Kuno National Park
2. Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary
3. Banni grasslands
How many of the above are located in Madhya Pradesh?
questions.why: Kuno is in Sheopur district. Gandhi Sagar and Nauradehi are also in Madhya Pradesh, while the Banni grasslands are in Kutch, Gujarat. Grassland and savanna ecosystems need protection because they are often overlooked.
questions.insight: Grassland and savanna ecosystems need protection, since they are often overlooked.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: A May 2026 Government release names areas for the next phase of Project Cheetah, beyond Kuno National Park. Which one of the following is among them?
opts: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve in Tamil Nadu and Kerala
The Thar desert dunes of Jaisalmer in Rajasthan
The Sundarbans delta in West Bengal
questions.why: The release names Banni, along with Gandhi Sagar and Nauradehi. Banni is Asia's largest tropical grassland.
questions.insight: Banni is Asia's largest tropical grassland.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to Pichavaram, consider the following statements:
1. It is a mangrove forest in West Bengal.
2. It is in Cuddalore district of Tamil Nadu.
3. It was designated a Ramsar site in 2022.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Pichavaram was designated a Ramsar site in 2022, together with Karikili Bird Sanctuary and Pallikaranai Marsh. The Sundarbans in West Bengal is India's largest mangrove area.
questions.insight: The Sundarbans in West Bengal is India's largest mangrove area.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: As per the India State of Forest Report 2023, India's mangrove cover was about which one of the following?
