opts: 12,000 sq km, about 0.4% of the country's area
50,000 sq km, about 1.5% of the country's area
499 sq km, about 0.015% of the country's area
4,992 sq km, about 0.15% of the country's area
questions.why: Mangrove cover rose by about 17 sq km from the 2019 assessment. The Forest Survey of India, Dehradun, publishes the report every two years.
questions.insight: The Forest Survey of India, Dehradun, publishes the report every two years.

src.name: PIB, India State of Forest Report 2023

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the MISHTI scheme (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes), consider the following statements:
1. It aims to restore and plant mangroves along the coast.
2. It runs from 2023-24 to 2027-28.
3. It is a scheme to protect coral reefs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: MISHTI targets about 540 sq km in nine coastal States and four Union Territories. Blue carbon ecosystems such as mangroves store large amounts of carbon.
questions.insight: Blue carbon ecosystems such as mangroves store large amounts of carbon.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Copernicus report that September 2026 was about 1.63°C above the pre-industrial average, consider the following statements:
1. It was the first time since November 2025 that two consecutive months were above 1.5°C.
2. The pre-industrial baseline used is 1950-1980.
3. A strong El Niño is adding to the warmth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The pre-industrial baseline is 1850-1900. The Paris Agreement aims to hold warming well below 2°C and pursue 1.5°C.
questions.insight: The Paris Agreement aims to hold warming well below 2°C and pursue 1.5°C.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A single year above 1.5°C between 2026 and 2030 does not by itself mean that the Paris Agreement's goal has failed.
Statement-II: The Paris goal refers to the long-term average warming over decades, not to a single year.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: The WMO estimates a 91% chance that at least one year in 2026-2030 will exceed 1.5°C above 1850-1900. The 2024 calendar year was the first to exceed 1.5°C.
questions.insight: The 2024 calendar year was the first to exceed 1.5°C.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Paris Agreement, consider the following statements:
1. It was adopted in 2015.
2. It aims to hold warming well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and to pursue 1.5°C.
3. Countries submit Nationally Determined Contributions to meet it.
4. It requires every country to limit warming to exactly 3°C.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: The Agreement sets no figure of 3°C. COP31 in Antalya (9 to 20 November 2026) begins the next stocktake cycle.
questions.insight: COP31 in Antalya (9 to 20 November 2026) begins the second global stocktake cycle.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the ICIMOD report of 2026 on glaciers in the Hindu Kush Himalaya, consider the following statements:
1. Glaciers have been losing ice at about double the rate since 2000.
2. Glacier area fell by about 12% between 1990 and 2020.
3. Glaciers are growing across the whole region.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Parts of the Himalayan cryosphere may be nearing irreversible retreat. Melting raises the risk of glacial lake outburst floods.
questions.insight: Melting raises the risk of glacial lake outburst floods.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: ICIMOD's HKH Snow Update 2026 reported that snow persistence was about 27.8% below the long-term average, the fourth straight year of decline.
Statement-II: Snowmelt supplies about three-fourths of the river water of the Hindu Kush Himalaya region.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Statement-II is incorrect: snowmelt supplies about a quarter of the region's river water. Repeated shortfalls raise the risk of water shortages and reduce groundwater and soil moisture.
questions.insight: Consecutive dry years also reduce groundwater and soil moisture.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), which tracks the Hindu Kush Himalaya, has its headquarters in which one of the following cities?
questions.why: ICIMOD's eight member countries are Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, Nepal and Pakistan. The Hindu Kush Himalaya is often called the 'Third Pole' because of its ice.
questions.insight: The Hindu Kush Himalaya is often called the 'Third Pole' because of its ice.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the greater one-horned rhino, consider the following statements:
1. The IUCN lists it as Vulnerable.
2. Kaziranga had about 2,613 in the 2022 count.
3. India's other rhino areas include Pobitora, Jaldapara, Gorumara and Dudhwa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Its numbers recovered from about 1,500 in the 1980s to over 4,000, mostly in Assam. World Rhino Day is observed on 22 September.
questions.insight: India's other rhino areas include Pobitora (Assam), Jaldapara and Gorumara (West Bengal) and Dudhwa (Uttar Pradesh).

src.name: PIB, Assam's role in protecting rhinos

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following rhino species:
1. Greater one-horned rhino
2. Javan rhino
3. Sumatran rhino
4. White rhino
How many of the above are found in India today?
questions.why: Javan rhinos once lived in India but are now found only in Indonesia. India holds the largest population of the greater one-horned rhino, and Nepal has the second largest.
questions.insight: India holds the largest population of the greater one-horned rhino; Nepal has the second largest.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) under the Convention on Biological Diversity, consider the following statements:
1. The ABS rules were set out by the Kyoto Protocol of 1997.
2. In India, the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 regulates ABS.
3. The National Biodiversity Authority is based in Chennai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Nagoya Protocol (2010) set out the ABS rules. Under ABS, benefits from using biological resources and traditional knowledge are shared fairly with the countries and communities that provide them.
questions.insight: CBD COP17 in Yerevan (19 to 30 October 2026) took up biodiversity decisions.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Green Climate Fund, set up under the UNFCCC to channel climate finance to developing countries, is headquartered in which one of the following?
opts: New York, in the United States of America
Nairobi, in the Republic of Kenya
Geneva, in the Swiss Confederation of Europe
questions.why: Its 46th Board meeting was held on 26 to 29 October 2026. In March 2026 the Board approved USD 960.3 million for 18 new projects. It is the largest dedicated climate fund for developing countries.
questions.insight: It is the largest dedicated climate fund for developing countries.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to India's National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in January 2019.
2. It aims to cut PM10 and PM2.5 levels in non-attainment cities.
3. It was launched in 2005.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The target was later raised to a 40% cut by 2025-26. The Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan ranking, released in September 2026, rates cities on their NCAP implementation.
questions.insight: 7 September is the International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Himalayan Monal, a colourful pheasant, consider the following statements:
1. It is the State bird of Uttarakhand.
2. It is the State bird of Himachal Pradesh.
3. Both it and the Western tragopan are Schedule I species under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Himachal Pradesh's State bird is the Western tragopan. The Monal lives in high-altitude forests of the Himalaya and is also called the Impeyan pheasant.
questions.insight: Both are Schedule I species under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Kasturirangan Committee (2013) recommended that the entire Western Ghats be declared an Ecologically Sensitive Area.
Statement-II: The Gadgil Committee (2011) had proposed that the entire Western Ghats be declared ecologically sensitive.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Statement-I is incorrect. The Kasturirangan Committee recommended that about 37% of the Western Ghats (roughly 60,000 sq km) be declared an Ecologically Sensitive Area, a softened version of the Gadgil proposal. Six States share the Western Ghats.
questions.insight: Six States share the Western Ghats: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

src.name: MoEFCC, Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Khair tree (Acacia catechu) is economically important because it yields which one of the following?
opts: Natural rubber used for tyres, tubes and industrial products
Cinchona bark, from which the drug quinine is extracted
Sandalwood oil used in perfumes, soaps and cosmetics
Katha (catechu) used with betel leaf, and hard timber
questions.why: Khair grows in dry deciduous forests and along riverbanks in the sub-Himalayan tract. Rubber comes from the Hevea tree and quinine from cinchona.
questions.insight: Rubber comes from the Hevea tree and quinine from cinchona.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider the following ports:
1. Deendayal (Kandla) Port
2. Paradip Port
3. V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin) Port
How many of the above are identified as green hydrogen hubs under India's National Green Hydrogen Mission?
questions.why: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy recognised the three major ports as green hydrogen hubs in October 2025. Deendayal Port is the old Kandla Port in Gujarat.
questions.insight: Deendayal Port is the old Kandla Port.

src.name: PIB, Three major ports recognised as Green Hydrogen hubs

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Permafrost is ground that stays at or below 0°C for at least how long?
questions.why: Thawing permafrost releases carbon dioxide and methane, which speeds up warming. Permafrost is found in the Arctic and in high mountains such as parts of the Himalaya.
questions.insight: Permafrost is found in the Arctic and in high mountains such as parts of the Himalaya.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to Census 2027, consider the following statements:
1. Castes are enumerated in the first, houselisting phase.
2. Houselisting runs from 1 April to 30 September 2026, with a 30-day window in each State or Union Territory.
3. The reference date for population enumeration is 1 March 2027.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Caste is enumerated in the second phase, population enumeration, which is held in February 2027 with 00:00 hours of 1 March 2027 as the reference date. Snow-bound areas such as Ladakh were to be counted in September 2026.
questions.insight: Castes will be enumerated in the second phase.

src.name: PIB, Registrar General of India, Census 2027

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to Census 2027, consider the following statements:
1. It is India's first digital census, with enumerators using mobile apps.
2. Households can self-enumerate for 15 days before the door-to-door visit.
3. It is run by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. More than 30 lakh enumerators and supervisors use the app, and the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, runs the census. The Election Commission has no role in it.
questions.insight: The Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, runs the census.

src.name: PIB, Registrar General of India, Census 2027

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following conditions for a settlement to be classified as a Census Town under the 1981 criteria:
1. A population of at least 5,000
2. At least 75% of male main workers in non-agricultural work
3. A density of at least 400 persons per sq km
4. A municipal corporation
How many of the above are required?
questions.why: A Census Town needs the first three conditions and has no municipality, so it stays administratively rural. A settlement with a municipality or similar body by law is a Statutory Town.
questions.insight: Many census towns lack urban local bodies, which limits their funds and services.

src.name: Census of India, concepts and definitions

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the National Single Window System (NSWS), which completed five years in September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It is administered by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade.
2. It was launched on 22 September 2021 as one portal for Central and State approvals.
3. The Reserve Bank of India grants all approvals on the portal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: DPIIT runs NSWS, launched on 22 September 2021 to give investors a single portal for approvals and clearances. The RBI does not grant its approvals. Industrial licences and entrepreneur memoranda have moved fully onto the portal.
questions.insight: Industrial licence and entrepreneur memorandum processes have moved fully onto NSWS.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Biometric Aadhaar Authentication rule for domestic LPG from 1 October 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Biometric authentication is required to book refills at the subsidised rate.
2. Consumers who do not complete it lose their LPG connection.
3. Consumers who do not complete it can still buy LPG at the market price.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Non-authenticated consumers keep the connection but pay the market price without subsidy. By 19 September 2026, 27.43 crore consumers (89.9%) had completed authentication. The subsidy reaches consumers by Direct Benefit Transfer under PAHAL.
questions.insight: LPG subsidy is paid by Direct Benefit Transfer under the PAHAL scheme.

src.name: PIB, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Aadhaar authentication can be made a condition for subsidies and benefits paid from the Consolidated Fund of India.
Statement-II: In the Puttaswamy case (2018), the Supreme Court upheld the use of Aadhaar for opening bank accounts and getting mobile connections.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Statement-I is correct under Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016. Statement-II is incorrect: the Court upheld Aadhaar for welfare but struck down its compulsory use by private entities such as banks and telecom companies.
questions.insight: In the Puttaswamy case (2018) the Supreme Court upheld Aadhaar for welfare but limited its use for private services.

src.name: PIB, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the DDU-GKY 2.0 guidelines of the Ministry of Rural Development, consider the following statements:
1. The minimum placement period is six months, up from three.
2. Placed trainees are tracked for 12 months.
3. The scheme trains only urban youth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: DDU-GKY is for rural youth aged 15 to 35, with a minimum 576-hour training course. It received Rs 750 crore in Budget 2026-27.
questions.insight: DDU-GKY began in 2014 and is observed on Antyodaya Diwas.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Ayurveda Day, which the Ministry of Ayush leads every year, is correct?
opts: It is observed on 1 January each year, as the first day of the calendar year
It is observed on Dhanteras, so its date changes every year with the lunar calendar
It is observed on 21 June each year, together with the International Day of Yoga
It is observed on 23 September each year, near the autumnal equinox
questions.why: The Government fixed 23 September as the permanent date, replacing Dhanteras and Dhanwantari Jayanti. The Ministry of Ayush leads the day.
questions.insight: The first Ayurveda Day was observed in 2016.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Attorney General for India, consider the following statements:
1. The Attorney General is appointed by the President under Article 76.
2. A person must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge to be appointed.
3. The Attorney General has the right to vote in Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President and has the right to speak in and take part in the proceedings of Parliament (Article 88), but cannot vote.
questions.insight: The Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General assist the Attorney General.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court.
Statement-II: The Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee under the 2023 Act.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, but the appointment procedure does not explain the removal protection. Removal needs a special majority in both Houses on proved misbehaviour or incapacity (Article 324(5)), which protects the Commission's independence.
questions.insight: This protects the Commission's independence.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following persons:
1. The Prime Minister
2. A Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
3. The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha
How many of the above are members of the committee that recommends appointments of the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners under the 2023 Act?
questions.why: The 2023 Act replaced the Chief Justice of India, whom the Supreme Court had placed on the panel earlier in 2023, with a Union Cabinet Minister. The President appoints on the committee's recommendation.
questions.insight: The President appoints on the committee's recommendation.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following persons:
1. A person who has been a judge of a High Court for at least five years
2. An advocate of a High Court for at least ten years
3. A person who has been a district judge for seven years
How many of the above are qualified for appointment as a Supreme Court judge under Article 124(3)?
questions.why: Article 124(3) also allows a distinguished jurist in the President's opinion. There is no category for a district judge of seven years. Appointments follow the Collegium system laid down in the Second and Third Judges cases.
questions.insight: Appointments follow the Collegium system laid down in the Second and Third Judges cases.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The 99th Constitutional Amendment (2014), which created the National Judicial Appointments Commission, was struck down by the Supreme Court in 2015.
Statement-II: The Court held that the NJAC violated the independence of the judiciary, a part of the basic structure.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: In the Fourth Judges Case (2015) the Court held that the NJAC compromised judicial independence, which led to the Collegium system being restored. The Supreme Court Collegium has the Chief Justice and the four senior-most judges.
questions.insight: The Collegium for the Supreme Court includes the CJI and four senior-most judges.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, consider the following statements:
1. An Internal Committee must be set up at a workplace with 10 or more employees.
2. Where there are fewer than 10 employees, complaints can be made only to the police.
3. The Act applies only to government offices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Smaller workplaces use a Local Committee at the district level, and the Act covers private and public workplaces. It gives statutory form to the Vishaka Guidelines (1997) laid down in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan.
questions.insight: The Vishaka case is Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Which one of the following is a right of an arrested person under Article 22(1) of the Constitution?
opts: To be released on bail in every case of arrest, whatever the nature of the offence
To be tried by a magistrate within 24 hours of the arrest, as the Constitution requires
To remain silent before a magistrate but to answer every question put by the police
To be informed of the grounds of arrest and to consult a lawyer of choice
questions.why: Article 22(2) separately requires production before a magistrate within 24 hours, which is not the same as trial. The Supreme Court has held that the grounds should be given in writing in a language the person understands.
questions.insight: Article 22 also lays down safeguards for preventive detention, with an Advisory Board for detention beyond three months.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Election Commission can deregister any political party that loses elections.
Statement-II: In Indian National Congress (I) v. Institute of Social Welfare (2002), the Supreme Court held that the Commission has no general power to deregister a party.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Statement-I is incorrect. The Court held that the Commission can deregister only in limited cases, such as registration obtained by fraud or a party declared unlawful. The Commission registers parties under Section 29A of the RP Act, 1951.
questions.insight: The ECI registers parties under Section 29A of the RP Act, 1951.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, the process of determining the nature and extent of forest rights is initiated by which one of the following?
questions.why: The Act recognises individual and community rights, including rights over minor forest produce. Its nodal ministry is the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
questions.insight: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 was renamed the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam in 2023.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Article 243A of the Constitution provides that the Gram Sabha may exercise such powers and perform such functions at the village level as the:
opts: President may specify by an order for each State
Parliament may by law provide for the whole country
Governor may specify by a notification in each district
Legislature of a State may by law provide
questions.why: Part IX, added by the 73rd Amendment (1992), makes the Gram Sabha the base of the three-tier Panchayati Raj system. Gram Panchayat Development Plans are approved in it.
questions.insight: The Panchayati Raj Ministry's Gram Panchayat Development Plans are approved in the Gram Sabha.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following schemes:
1. Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana
2. PM-KISAN
3. MGNREGA
4. Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana
How many of the above were merged to form the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY)?
questions.why: PM-AJAY, from 2021-22, merged the Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana, the Special Central Assistance to the SC Sub-Plan and the Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment runs it.
questions.insight: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment runs it.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958, consider the following statements:
1. The Act applies automatically to every State in the country.
2. The Act can be applied only after an area is declared a 'disturbed area'.
3. The declaration can be made by the Central Government or the Governor of the State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Section 3 provides for the declaration. AFSPA has been withdrawn from several areas, for example Tripura in 2015 and Meghalaya in 2018.
questions.insight: AFSPA has been withdrawn from several areas, such as Tripura (2015) and Meghalaya (2018).

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following forces:
1. COBRA
2. Rapid Action Force
3. Greyhounds
How many of the above are specialised units of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF)?
questions.why: COBRA (Commando Battalion for Resolute Action), raised in 2008-09 for jungle warfare against Maoists, and the Rapid Action Force are units of the CRPF. Greyhounds is the Andhra Pradesh police's anti-Naxal force.
questions.insight: Left-Wing Extremism is concentrated in the 'Red Corridor'.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: In which one of the following did Maoists attack a Congress convoy in the Jhiram Ghati of Bastar, killing 27 people?
questions.why: The ambush hit a convoy returning from a 'Parivartan Rally' on 25 May 2013. The NIA, set up under the NIA Act, 2008 after 26/11, investigated it.
questions.insight: The NIA, set up under the NIA Act, 2008 after 26/11, investigated the attack.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the 'RAKSHA' document released by the Defence Minister on 3 September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It is a ten-year roadmap for India's defence diplomacy.
2. It is a defence treaty signed between India and Sri Lanka.
3. Its pillars include defence exports and a larger maritime role as a net security provider.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: RAKSHA's pillars are strategic partnerships, capacity building through exercises and training, indigenous defence exports and maritime security. It complements the MAHASAGAR vision.
questions.insight: It complements the MAHASAGAR vision, which stands for Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the visit of the Vietnamese leader To Lam to India in May 2026, consider the following statements:
1. India and Vietnam raised their relationship to an Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
2. The visit took place from 5 to 7 May 2026.
3. An MoU between IREL and a Vietnamese institute on rare earths was among the outcomes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The outcomes also included an RBI and State Bank of Vietnam MoU on payments. Vietnam is a key partner in India's Act East Policy.
questions.insight: Vietnam is a key partner in India's Act East Policy and Indo-Pacific vision.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the India–EU Free Trade Agreement, consider the following statements:
1. Negotiations were concluded on 27 January 2026.
2. India gets preferential access for over 99% of its exports by trade value to the EU.
3. The EU made commitments across 144 services subsectors.
4. India opened its dairy, cereal and poultry sectors fully to EU imports.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India protected sensitive sectors such as dairy, cereals and poultry. Negotiations were relaunched in 2022 after a pause since 2013.
questions.insight: Negotiations were relaunched in 2022 after a pause since 2013.

src.name: PIB, Ministry of Commerce, India-EU FTA

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the launch of talks between India and MERCOSUR on 14 September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The two sides launched negotiations to expand their existing Preferential Trade Agreement.
2. Uruguay held the MERCOSUR pro tempore presidency at the time.
3. The two sides signed a free trade agreement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Terms of Reference for the expanded agreement were still being finalised, so no agreement was signed.
questions.insight: MERCOSUR's full members are Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay (Venezuela is suspended; Bolivia is acceding).

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Brazil
2. Chile
3. Peru
How many of the above are full members of MERCOSUR?
questions.why: MERCOSUR's full members are Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay (Venezuela is suspended; Bolivia is acceding). Chile and Peru are associate states. MERCOSUR was founded by the Treaty of Asuncion (1991).
questions.insight: MERCOSUR was founded by the Treaty of Asunción (1991).

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), consider the following statements:
1. The SCO was founded in 2017.
2. India became a full member in 2017 along with Pakistan.
3. The SCO secretariat is in Beijing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The founding members were China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and, from 2001, Uzbekistan. The Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure is in Tashkent. The 26th summit was held in Bishkek on 31 August and 1 September 2026.
questions.insight: Founding members were China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and (from 2001) Uzbekistan.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: Which one of the following sets of countries formed the original BRIC grouping, before South Africa joined in 2010?
opts: The United States, the United Kingdom, Japan and Germany
Brazil, Russia, India, China and Iran
questions.why: The term 'BRIC' was coined by the economist Jim O'Neill in 2001, and the first leaders' summit was in 2009. India chairs BRICS in 2026.
questions.insight: India chaired BRICS in 2026.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS, 1982), consider the following statements:
1. A coastal state's Exclusive Economic Zone extends up to 200 nautical miles from the baseline.
2. The territorial sea extends up to 24 nautical miles.
3. The contiguous zone extends up to 24 nautical miles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The territorial sea is 12 nautical miles. The continental shelf can extend to 350 nautical miles under conditions. India ratified UNCLOS in 1995.
questions.insight: India ratified UNCLOS in 1995.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The principle of 'innocent passage' for foreign ships under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea applies in which one of the following?
questions.why: Foreign ships may pass through the territorial sea if they do not harm the peace, order or security of the coastal state. Ships have freedom of navigation in the EEZ and on the high seas.
questions.insight: Ships have the freedom of navigation in the EEZ and on the high seas.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Indus Waters Treaty (1960) between India and Pakistan was brokered with the World Bank as a signatory.
Statement-II: The Treaty gives India the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas and Sutlej) and Pakistan the three western rivers (Indus, Jhelum and Chenab).
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, but the division of rivers does not explain the World Bank's role. India has limited use of the western rivers. A Court of Arbitration issued an award in August 2026 on the Treaty's provisions.
questions.insight: A Court of Arbitration issued an award in August 2026 on the treaty's provisions.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to defence cooperation between India and the United States, consider the following statements:
1. The Defence Technology and Trade Initiative (DTTI) was launched in 2012.
2. The DTTI aims to co-produce and co-develop defence items such as the Javelin anti-tank missile.
3. India has signed COMCASA, LEMOA and BECA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India has in fact signed all four foundational agreements: GSOMIA (2002), LEMOA (2016), COMCASA (2018) and BECA (2020).
questions.insight: DTTI was launched in 2012 to co-produce and co-develop defence items.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Japan
2. Australia
3. South Korea
How many of the above are members of the Quad?
questions.why: The Quad groups India, the United States, Japan and Australia and focuses on a free and open Indo-Pacific, with working groups on health, technology and maritime domain awareness. AUKUS is a different arrangement: Australia, the UK and the US.
questions.insight: AUKUS is a different arrangement: Australia, UK and US.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India's current account deficit in the first quarter of 2026-27 was only US$4.2 billion, or 0.5% of GDP, despite a merchandise trade deficit of about US$86 billion.
Statement-II: Remittances of US$42.9 billion and receipts from services offset much of the merchandise trade deficit.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, and the second explains the first. India is the world's largest recipient of remittances, which keeps the current account gap small.
questions.insight: India is the world's largest recipient of remittances.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections, consider the following statements:
1. Gross GST collections for April to September 2026 were about Rs 12.46 lakh crore, up 11.6% over the year before.
2. The number of registered GST taxpayers has fallen to about 60 lakh.
3. GST has been in force since 1 July 2017 under the 101st Constitutional Amendment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Registered taxpayers have risen from around 60 lakh in 2017 to about 1.70 crore in September 2026, not fallen.
questions.insight: GST has been in force since 1 July 2017 under the 101st Constitutional Amendment.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the GST Council, consider the following statements:
1. It is a constitutional body under Article 279A.
2. The Centre has one-third and the States two-thirds of the weighted votes.
3. Decisions are taken by a simple majority of the weighted votes.
4. It is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Decisions need three-fourths of the weighted votes, not a simple majority. Article 246A gives both Parliament and State legislatures the power to make GST laws.
questions.insight: Article 246A gives both Parliament and State legislatures the power to make GST laws.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the RBI, consider the following statements:
1. It has six members.
2. Three members are from the RBI and three are external members appointed by the Government.
3. The Union Finance Minister has the casting vote in case of a tie.
4. The RBI Governor has the casting vote in case of a tie.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: The Governor, as chairperson, has the casting vote. The MPC targets CPI inflation of 4% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%.
questions.insight: The MPC targets CPI inflation of 4% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the RBI's policy rates, consider the following statements:
1. The standing deposit facility (SDF) rate sits 25 basis points below the repo rate.
2. The marginal standing facility (MSF) rate sits 25 basis points above the repo rate.
3. The CRR is the rate at which banks borrow from the RBI against government securities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The repo rate is the rate at which banks borrow from the RBI against government securities. The CRR is the share of deposits banks must keep with the RBI. The MPC kept the repo rate at 5.25% in June 2026 and the RBI raised it to 5.50% in October 2026.
questions.insight: The RBI raised the repo rate to 5.50% in October 2026.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Under the Statutory Liquidity Ratio, banks must hold a share of their deposits in liquid assets such as government securities, gold and cash.
Statement-II: Under the Cash Reserve Ratio, banks must keep a share of their deposits with the RBI.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, but the CRR does not explain the SLR. SLR assets are held by the banks themselves; CRR is held with the RBI. The statutory ceiling for SLR is 40% of net demand and time liabilities.
questions.insight: The statutory SLR ceiling is 40% of net demand and time liabilities.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999, administered by the Ministry of Finance, replaced which one of the following earlier laws?
opts: The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, as amended
The Companies Act, 1956, as amended later
questions.why: FEMA made foreign exchange violations civil rather than criminal matters. The RBI and the Directorate of Enforcement play key roles.
questions.insight: FEMA is administered by the Ministry of Finance.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003, consider the following statements:
1. It seeks to bring fiscal discipline by setting targets for the fiscal deficit and debt.
2. The N.K. Singh Committee (2017) recommended a debt-to-GDP target of 60% for the General Government.
3. Escape clauses allow deviations for reasons such as war, national calamity or severe slowdown.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Committee also suggested a debt-to-GDP target of 40% for the Centre.
questions.insight: Escape clauses allow deviations for reasons such as war, national calamity or severe slowdown.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following bodies:
1. Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices
2. NITI Aayog
3. Finance Commission
4. Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs
How many of the above are directly involved in recommending or approving the Minimum Support Price?
questions.why: The CACP recommends MSP for 22 mandated crops and the Fair and Remunerative Price for sugarcane. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approves it, and the Food Corporation of India procures foodgrains at MSP for the buffer stock.
questions.insight: FCI procures foodgrains at MSP for the buffer stock.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, held in September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Its theme is 'Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations that Delivers for All'.
2. The General Assembly has 193 member states, each with one vote.
3. The votes of member states are weighted by their contribution to the UN budget.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Each member state has one vote regardless of size or contribution. India's External Affairs Minister spoke in the General Debate in late September on the reform of the international order.
questions.insight: The UNGA has 193 member states, each with one vote.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Brazil
2. Germany
3. India
How many of the above are members of the G4 group that pushes for reform of the UN Security Council?
questions.why: The fourth member is Japan. The G4 seek permanent seats for each other, while the Uniting for Consensus group, led by Italy and Pakistan, opposes new permanent seats. India says new permanent members must have the same rights, including the veto, as the existing ones.
questions.insight: India says new permanent members must hold the same rights, including the veto, as the existing ones.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the United Nations Security Council, consider the following statements:
1. The five permanent members are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States.
2. There are ten elected non-permanent members, who serve five-year terms.
3. A veto by any permanent member blocks a substantive resolution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Non-permanent members serve two-year terms. Germany is not a permanent member.
questions.insight: A veto by any P5 member blocks a substantive resolution.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the non-permanent members of the UN Security Council, consider the following statements:
1. They are elected by the General Assembly for five years.
2. Five of them are elected each year.
3. A retiring member cannot be re-elected immediately.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The term is two years. India served its eighth term in 2021-22.
questions.insight: India served its eighth term in 2021-22.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The International Court of Justice has its seat in The Hague.
Statement-II: The International Criminal Court, which also sits in The Hague, is a principal organ of the United Nations.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Statement-II is incorrect: the ICC is not a UN organ. The ICJ is the principal judicial organ of the UN and has 15 judges elected for nine-year terms.
questions.insight: The International Criminal Court, also in The Hague, is not a UN organ.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The International Atomic Energy Agency, which verifies that nuclear material is used for peaceful purposes, has its headquarters in:
questions.why: The IAEA administers safeguards. The Nuclear Suppliers Group, which India has been seeking to join, decides on exports of nuclear materials.
questions.insight: The Nuclear Suppliers Group, which India has been seeking to join, decides on export of nuclear materials.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: Peninsular India is separated from Sri Lanka by the Palk Strait and which one of the following?
questions.why: Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu) lies between Rameswaram and Mannar, and Katchatheevu island lies in the Palk Strait. The 1974 and 1976 agreements fixed the maritime boundary between India and Sri Lanka.
questions.insight: The 1974 and 1976 agreements fixed the maritime boundary between India and Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project, consider the following statements:
1. It links Kolkata to Sittwe port in Myanmar.
2. It is the same project as the India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway.
3. It connects India with Bangladesh through the port of Chittagong.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: From Sittwe the project continues by river and road to Mizoram, giving the Northeast another route. The Trilateral Highway is a separate project.
questions.insight: The India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway is a separate project.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Durand Line is the boundary between Afghanistan and Pakistan.
Statement-II: The Durand Line was drawn in 1893 between British India and Afghanistan.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, and the second explains the first: Pakistan inherited the line from British India. Afghanistan has not recognised it as an international border. The McMahon Line concerns India and China, and the Radcliffe Line India and Pakistan.
questions.insight: The McMahon Line concerns India and China, and the Radcliffe Line India and Pakistan.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following Indian States:
1. Manipur
2. Mizoram
3. Tripura
4. Meghalaya
How many of the above share a border with Bangladesh?
questions.why: The States bordering Bangladesh are West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Manipur borders Myanmar. The India-Bangladesh land boundary was settled by the 2015 Land Boundary Agreement.
questions.insight: India–Bangladesh land boundary was settled by the 2015 Land Boundary Agreement.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The Pravasi Bharatiya Divas, observed by the Ministry of External Affairs, is celebrated every year on which one of the following dates?
questions.why: The day marks Mahatma Gandhi's return to India from South Africa in 1915.
questions.insight: It is observed by the Ministry of External Affairs.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), consider the following statements:
1. ASEAN has ten members.
2. Timor-Leste became the 11th member in October 2025.
3. The ASEAN Secretariat is in Jakarta.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India's Act East Policy is built on ASEAN centrality.
questions.insight: India's Act East Policy is built on ASEAN centrality.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Consumer Price Index (CPI) release for August 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The CPI now uses 2024=100 as the base year.
2. Food inflation on the Consumer Food Price Index was 5.95%.
3. Tomato prices rose by about 31% over the year.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: Combined retail inflation was 4.82% (provisional). Onion inflation jumped to about 48%, while tomato prices fell by about 31%. The RBI's target is 4% with a band of 2% to 6%.
questions.insight: The RBI's inflation target is 4% with a band of 2% to 6%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which one of the following compiles and releases the Consumer Price Index (CPI) in India?
opts: The Office of the Economic Adviser, in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry of the Government
The Reserve Bank of India, through its Monetary Policy Department in Mumbai
NITI Aayog, through its Data and Analysis Division in the Government of India
The National Statistics Office, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.why: The Wholesale Price Index is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The RBI uses CPI (Combined) for its inflation target.
questions.insight: The RBI uses CPI (Combined) for its inflation target.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to India's GDP estimate for April to June 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The National Statistics Office released the estimate on 1 September 2026.
2. Real GDP is measured at the constant prices of the new base year, 2022-23.
3. Gross Value Added is higher than GDP by the amount of net product taxes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: GDP equals Gross Value Added plus net product taxes (taxes less subsidies on products), so GVA is lower than GDP when taxes exceed subsidies.
questions.insight: Gross Value Added differs from GDP by net product taxes.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, consider the following statements:
1. The Committee of Creditors approves a resolution plan by a simple majority of 51% of the voting share.
2. The 2019 amendment lowered the threshold from 75% to 66%.
3. The National Company Law Tribunal is the adjudicating authority for companies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The approval threshold is 66% of the voting share. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) regulates insolvency professionals.
questions.insight: The IBBI regulates insolvency professionals.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), consider the following statements:
1. It was set up administratively in 1988.
2. It became a statutory body under the Companies Act, 2013.
3. Appeals against its orders are heard by the Securities Appellate Tribunal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: SEBI became a statutory body in 1992 under the SEBI Act, 1992, not under the Companies Act, 2013.
questions.insight: The Securities Appellate Tribunal hears appeals against SEBI orders.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body that is constituted every two years under Article 148.
Statement-II: The recommendations of the Finance Commission are advisory and not binding on the Government.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Statement-I is incorrect: the Commission is constituted every five years under Article 280 (Article 148 is the Comptroller and Auditor General). The 16th Finance Commission, headed by Arvind Panagariya, reports for 2026-27 to 2030-31.
questions.insight: Its recommendations are advisory, not binding.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Domestic commercial banks must lend 40% of adjusted net bank credit to priority sectors such as agriculture, MSMEs, education and housing.
Statement-II: Small finance banks have a lower priority-sector target than domestic commercial banks.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Statement-II is incorrect: small finance banks have a higher target of 75%.
questions.insight: Small finance banks have a higher target of 75%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), consider the following statements:
1. It is operated directly by the Reserve Bank of India.
2. It is run by the National Payments Corporation of India, an umbrella organisation for retail payments.
3. The same organisation also runs RuPay.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: NPCI was set up by the RBI and the Indian Banks' Association. The RBI regulates payment systems under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, but does not run UPI itself.
questions.insight: The RBI regulates payment systems under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Kisan Credit Card scheme is meant to provide farmers with which one of the following?
opts: Free tractors and other farm machinery for every landholding farmer
Land pattas and title deeds for every landless agricultural worker
Crop insurance cover for loss of the crop in natural calamities only
Short-term crop and allied-activity credit at concessional interest
questions.why: Timely repayment earns an interest subvention that lowers the effective interest rate. NABARD refinances rural credit.
questions.insight: NABARD refinances rural credit.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The World Trade Organization, headquartered in Geneva, replaced the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) in which year?
questions.why: The Ministerial Conference is its highest decision-making body and meets at least every two years. The Appellate Body of its dispute settlement system has been non-functional since 2019.
questions.insight: The WTO dispute settlement body's Appellate Body has been non-functional since 2019.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
Consider the following items in the Union Budget:
1. Recovery of loans
2. Corporation tax
3. Interest received on loans
4. Proceeds of disinvestment
How many of the above are capital receipts?
questions.why: Capital receipts create a liability or reduce an asset: borrowings, loan recoveries and disinvestment. Corporation tax is a revenue receipt, and so is interest received on loans.
questions.insight: The fiscal deficit equals total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation is based in Tashkent.
Statement-II: The secretariat of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation is in Beijing.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, but the location of the secretariat does not explain the location of the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure. India joined the SCO as a full member in 2017.
questions.insight: India joined the SCO as a full member in 2017.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), consider the following statements:
1. They were set up under the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976.
2. They are regulated under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 and not owned by any government.
3. The Centre holds 50% of their shares, the sponsor bank 35% and the State 15%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: RRBs are owned jointly by the Centre, the sponsor bank and the State. The Narasimham Working Group recommended them in 1975.
questions.insight: The Narasimham Working Group recommended them in 1975.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: In public finance, Zero-Based Budgeting, as against incremental budgeting, means which one of the following?
opts: The budget is balanced with a fiscal deficit of zero in that year
No new taxes are levied and only the existing taxes continue
Every expense must be justified afresh in each budget cycle
Ministries receive an automatic increase over last year's allocation
questions.why: Incremental budgeting adds to the previous year's base. Outcome budgeting links spending to measurable results.
questions.insight: Outcome budgeting links spending to measurable results.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
Consider the following rivers:
1. Narmada
2. Mahanadi
3. Krishna
How many of the above flow west and drain into the Arabian Sea?
questions.why: The Narmada and the Tapi flow west through rift valleys. The Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi flow east to the Bay of Bengal. The Narmada originates at Amarkantak.
questions.insight: The Narmada originates at Amarkantak.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The 'Loo', experienced in the northern plains in May and June, is which one of the following?
opts: A cold wave that blows down from the Himalayas during the winter months
A monsoon current that brings rain to the north-western plains
A winter cyclone that forms over the Arabian Sea and the Bay
A hot, dry wind blowing in the afternoon from the Thar side
questions.why: Western disturbances, not the Loo, bring winter rain to the north-west.
questions.insight: Western disturbances bring winter rain to the north-west.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the Western Ghats, consider the following statements:
1. They are also known as the Satpura range.
2. They are known officially as Sahyadri.
3. They have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2012.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala is the highest peak in the range. The Eastern Ghats are older and more broken.
questions.insight: The Eastern Ghats are older and more broken.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Black cotton soil (regur), formed from basalt in the Deccan Plateau, is best suited for which one of the following crops?
questions.why: It holds moisture well. Its clay content makes it swell and crack with changes in moisture.
questions.insight: Its clay content makes it swell and crack with moisture changes.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Sanchi Stupa, consider the following statements:
1. It was originally built under Emperor Ashoka.
2. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1989.
3. Its gateways (toranas) were added in the Maurya period.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The gateways were added later, in the Satavahana period. Sanchi is in Madhya Pradesh.
questions.insight: The gateways (toranas) were added later in the Satavahana period.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Battle of Plassey (1757) started British political control in Bengal.
Statement-II: Mir Jafar's betrayal of Siraj-ud-Daulah helped the Company led by Robert Clive to win.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: The battle was fought between the British East India Company and Siraj-ud-Daulah, Nawab of Bengal.
questions.insight: It started British political control in Bengal.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 achieved a soft landing in 2023 near which part of the Moon?
questions.why: India became the first country to land near the lunar south pole, on 23 August 2023. National Space Day is observed on 23 August.
questions.insight: National Space Day is observed on 23 August.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, consider the following statements:
1. Data fiduciaries must process personal data with the consent of the person, with some exceptions.
2. Data fiduciaries must store all personal data abroad.
3. Individuals whose data is processed are called 'data principals'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Act does not require data to be stored abroad. The Data Protection Board of India hears complaints.
questions.insight: Individuals are called 'data principals'.
